title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Prohibiting the Sealing Up, Freezing, and Deduction of Social Insurance Funds in the Hearing and Execution of Civil and Economic Dispute Cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Not Sealing, Freezing, or Deducting Social Insurance Funds When Hearing and Enforcing Civil and Economic Dispute Cases

Fa [2000] No. 19

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

In the recent period, a small number of courts, when hearing and enforcing economic dispute cases between former subordinate enterprises of social insurance agencies (all of which have now been fully separated) and other enterprises or entities, have sealed the social insurance fund accounts opened by the social insurance agencies, thereby affecting the normal disbursement of social insurance funds and adversely affecting social stability. To prevent the recurrence of such situations, notice is hereby given as follows:

Social insurance funds are public funds managed by social insurance agencies on behalf of the insured persons and ultimately enjoyed by the insured persons; they are not owned by the social insurance agencies. The social insurance agencies establish special accounts for the management of such funds, which are to be used exclusively for specified purposes, specifically to guarantee the basic living needs of retired enterprise employees and unemployed persons. These are special-purpose funds and shall not be diverted for other uses. Therefore, when hearing and enforcing civil and economic dispute cases, people's courts at all levels shall not seal, freeze, or deduct social insurance funds; nor shall they use social insurance funds to repay the debts of the social insurance agencies or their former subordinate enterprises.

If any people's court discovers violations of the above provisions, it shall promptly make corrections in accordance with the law.

February 18, 2000
